title: Dairy products, calcium, and prostate cancer risk: a systematic review and meta-analysis of cohort studies
authors: Aune D, Navarro Rosenblatt DA, Chan DS, Vieira AR, Vieira R, Greenwood DC, et al.
population: 32 prospective studies; searches to April 2013; World Cancer Research Fund/American Institute for Cancer Research Continuous Update Project
funder: Supported by the World Cancer Research Fund (grant 2007/SP01) as part of the Continuous Update Project.
result: Total prostate cancer, summary RR: total dairy products 1.07 (95% CI 1.02 to 1.12; 15 studies) per 400 g/day; total milk 1.03 (1.00 to 1.07; 14 studies) per 200 g/day; cheese 1.09 (1.02 to 1.18; 11 studies) per 50 g/day; dietary calcium 1.05 (1.02 to 1.09; 15 studies) per 400 mg/day. Dairy calcium, but not nondairy or supplemental calcium, was positively associated with total prostate cancer.
